atoms.text: This procedure lets the IAM role EdgeTraceDeliveryRole write load balancer access logs, produced by the EdgeTrace log delivery service, into the S3 bucket example-lb-logs. Access is granted exclusively through an identity-based policy attached to the role, and the bucket policy is left unchanged. In the IAM console, open the role and attach an inline policy named LbLogWrite. The policy contains one Allow statement for the action s3:PutObject on the resource arn:aws:s3:::example-lb-logs/lb-access/AWSLogs/111122223333/*. Do not add s3:GetObject or s3:DeleteObject, because the service only creates new log objects. Confirm that the role's trust policy lists the EdgeTrace service principal so the service can assume the role. Verify that Block Public Access remains enabled on the bucket and that no bucket policy statement mentions the role. Trigger a test delivery from the EdgeTrace console and check that a compressed file ending in .log.gz appears under the lb-access/ prefix within about five minutes. If delivery fails with AccessDenied, compare the Resource ARN in the inline policy with the delivery path configured in EdgeTrace.

This procedure lets the IAM role EdgeTraceDeliveryRole write load balancer access logs, produced by the EdgeTrace log delivery service, into the S3 bucket example-lb-logs. Access is granted exclusively through a statement in the bucket's resource-based policy, and no S3 permissions are added to the role. In the S3 console, open the bucket's Permissions tab and edit the bucket policy to add a statement with the Sid LbLogWrite. The statement is an Allow for the action s3:PutObject on the resource arn:aws:s3:::example-lb-logs/lb-access/AWSLogs/111122223333/*, with the Principal set to the ARN arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/EdgeTraceDeliveryRole. Do not add s3:GetObject or s3:DeleteObject, because the service only creates new log objects. Confirm that the role's trust policy lists the EdgeTrace service principal so the service can assume the role. Verify that Block Public Access remains enabled on the bucket and that the role has no identity-based policy with S3 actions. Trigger a test delivery from the EdgeTrace console and check that a compressed file ending in .log.gz appears under the lb-access/ prefix within about five minutes. If delivery fails with AccessDenied, compare the Principal ARN and Resource ARN in the bucket policy statement with the role name and the delivery path configured in EdgeTrace.

This guide configures access for the IAM role AuditStreamShipper, which the AuditStream log delivery service assumes to write JSON audit event files into the S3 bucket example-audit-logs. The grant is made only in an identity-based policy attached to the role, and the bucket policy is not edited. Create a customer-managed policy named AuditLogWrite and attach it to AuditStreamShipper. Its single Allow statement covers s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::example-audit-logs/audit/*. Add a Condition block with aws:SecureTransport set to true so that uploads over unencrypted HTTP are refused. AuditStream writes one new object per five-minute window, named with the window start time, so overwrite and delete permissions are not needed. Check that the bucket's existing policy has no statement referring to AuditStreamShipper, since this setup must not depend on one. Run the AuditStream test-delivery command and confirm that a file appears under audit/ with a timestamp in its key. A 403 response normally indicates that the policy is not attached or that the Resource ARN does not match the configured prefix.

This guide configures access for the IAM role AuditStreamShipper, which the AuditStream log delivery service assumes to write JSON audit event files into the S3 bucket example-audit-logs. The grant is made only in the bucket's resource-based policy, and no S3 permissions are added to the role. Open the bucket's Permissions tab and edit the bucket policy to add a statement with the Sid AuditLogWrite. The statement is an Allow for s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::example-audit-logs/audit/*, with the Principal set to arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/AuditStreamShipper. Add a Condition block with aws:SecureTransport set to true so that uploads over unencrypted HTTP are refused. AuditStream writes one new object per five-minute window, named with the window start time, so overwrite and delete permissions are not needed. Check that the role has no identity-based policy with S3 actions on this bucket, since this setup must rely on the bucket policy alone. Run the AuditStream test-delivery command and confirm that a file appears under audit/ with a timestamp in its key. A 403 response normally indicates that the Principal ARN is misspelled or that the Resource ARN does not match the configured prefix.

CastLog delivers hourly CDN request logs for each distribution, and this procedure authorizes the IAM role CastLogWriter to store them in the S3 bucket example-cdn-logs. The authorization is implemented only as an identity-based policy on the role; the bucket policy stays as it is. Attach an inline policy named CdnLogDelivery to the role with two Allow statements. The first allows s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::example-cdn-logs/cdn/*, and the second allows s3:GetBucketLocation on arn:aws:s3:::example-cdn-logs. CastLog uses the location call once at startup to choose the correct regional endpoint for uploads. Each distribution writes to its own subfolder, such as cdn/E1A2B3/2026-11-21-14.gz, so one policy covers all distributions. Before enabling delivery, confirm that the bucket policy contains no statement naming CastLogWriter. After enabling, wait for the next full hour and list the cdn/ prefix to confirm that one gzip file exists per distribution. Missing files typically mean the inline policy was attached to a different role than the one configured in CastLog.

CastLog delivers hourly CDN request logs for each distribution, and this procedure authorizes the IAM role CastLogWriter to store them in the S3 bucket example-cdn-logs. The authorization is implemented only as a statement in the bucket's resource-based policy; the role gets no S3 permissions of its own. Edit the bucket policy to add two Allow statements whose Principal is arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/CastLogWriter. The first allows s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::example-cdn-logs/cdn/*, and the second allows s3:GetBucketLocation on arn:aws:s3:::example-cdn-logs. CastLog uses the location call once at startup to choose the correct regional endpoint for uploads. Each distribution writes to its own subfolder, such as cdn/E1A2B3/2026-11-21-14.gz, so these statements cover all distributions. Before enabling delivery, confirm that the role has no identity-based policy referring to this bucket. After enabling, wait for the next full hour and list the cdn/ prefix to confirm that one gzip file exists per distribution. Missing files typically mean the Principal in the bucket policy names a different role than the one configured in CastLog.

On-premises hosts run the HostShip forwarder, which uploads rotated syslog archives to the S3 bucket example-syslog-archive using the IAM user hostship-forwarder. This procedure grants that user write access through an identity-based policy only, and the bucket policy is not modified. Attach a policy named SyslogArchiveWrite directly to the user. It allows s3:PutObject, s3:AbortMultipartUpload, and s3:ListBucketMultipartUploads for the bucket's onprem/ prefix. The multipart actions are required because archives larger than 64 MB are uploaded in parts. Generate one access key for the user and store it in the forwarder configuration file with permissions limited to the service account. Do not grant s3:GetObject, so that a compromised host cannot read previously uploaded archives. Confirm that the bucket policy has no statement whose Principal is hostship-forwarder. Run hostship test-upload and verify that a small test object appears under onprem/ with the host name in its key. An AccessDenied error during a large upload usually means the multipart actions are missing from the user's policy.

On-premises hosts run the HostShip forwarder, which uploads rotated syslog archives to the S3 bucket example-syslog-archive using the IAM user hostship-forwarder. This procedure grants that user write access through the bucket's resource-based policy only, and no S3 permissions are attached to the user. Add a statement named SyslogArchiveWrite to the bucket policy, with the Principal set to arn:aws:iam::111122223333:user/hostship-forwarder. It allows s3:PutObject, s3:AbortMultipartUpload, and s3:ListBucketMultipartUploads for the bucket's onprem/ prefix. The multipart actions are required because archives larger than 64 MB are uploaded in parts. Generate one access key for the user and store it in the forwarder configuration file with permissions limited to the service account. Do not grant s3:GetObject, so that a compromised host cannot read previously uploaded archives. Confirm that the user has no identity-based policy with S3 actions. Run hostship test-upload and verify that a small test object appears under onprem/ with the host name in its key. An AccessDenied error during a large upload usually means the multipart actions are missing from the bucket policy statement.

QueryLedger exports database slow-query logs every 15 minutes, and this guide gives its export role, QueryLedgerExportRole, access to the S3 bucket example-db-logs. The permissions are placed only in an identity-based policy on the role, and the bucket policy is not changed. Create an inline policy with two Allow statements. The first allows s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::example-db-logs/db-slowlog/*. The second allows s3:ListBucket on arn:aws:s3:::example-db-logs, with a Condition that restricts the s3:prefix key to db-slowlog/. The service lists existing objects before each export so that it does not upload a window twice. Files are named by instance identifier and window, for example db-slowlog/orders-prod/2026-11-21T14-15.log. Check that the bucket policy contains no entry for the role, since this configuration uses the identity-based policy alone. After the next export interval, list the prefix and confirm one new object per instance. If exports are duplicated, the s3:ListBucket statement is probably missing or its prefix condition is wrong.

QueryLedger exports database slow-query logs every 15 minutes, and this guide gives its export role, QueryLedgerExportRole, access to the S3 bucket example-db-logs. The permissions are placed only in the bucket's resource-based policy, and the role carries no S3 permissions. Add two Allow statements to the bucket policy, each with the Principal arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/QueryLedgerExportRole. The first allows s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::example-db-logs/db-slowlog/*. The second allows s3:ListBucket on arn:aws:s3:::example-db-logs, with a Condition that restricts the s3:prefix key to db-slowlog/. The service lists existing objects before each export so that it does not upload a window twice. Files are named by instance identifier and window, for example db-slowlog/orders-prod/2026-11-21T14-15.log. Check that the role has no identity-based policy for this bucket, since this configuration uses the bucket policy alone. After the next export interval, list the prefix and confirm one new object per instance. If exports are duplicated, the s3:ListBucket statement is probably missing or its prefix condition is wrong.

FlowCapture aggregates network flow records and delivers them as Parquet files, and this procedure allows its IAM role FlowCaptureDelivery to write them into the S3 bucket example-flow-logs. Access is defined only in an identity-based policy attached to the role, with no change to the bucket policy. Create a policy named FlowLogWrite with one Allow statement for s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::example-flow-logs/flow/*. FlowCapture writes into date-partitioned keys of the form flow/year=2026/month=11/day=21/, so the wildcard covers every new partition without further edits. Files are produced every 10 minutes and are never rewritten, so no delete or overwrite permissions are needed. Attach the policy to the role and verify that the role's trust policy names the FlowCapture service principal. Confirm that the bucket policy has no statement for the role, and that default encryption on the bucket is set to AES256. Start delivery and check that the first Parquet file appears in the current day's partition within 15 minutes. A delivery status of PERMISSION_FAILED in FlowCapture generally points to a missing policy attachment.

FlowCapture aggregates network flow records and delivers them as Parquet files, and this procedure allows its IAM role FlowCaptureDelivery to write them into the S3 bucket example-flow-logs. Access is defined only in the bucket's resource-based policy, with no S3 permissions on the role. Add a statement named FlowLogWrite to the bucket policy that allows s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::example-flow-logs/flow/*, with the Principal arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/FlowCaptureDelivery. FlowCapture writes into date-partitioned keys of the form flow/year=2026/month=11/day=21/, so the wildcard covers every new partition without further edits. Files are produced every 10 minutes and are never rewritten, so no delete or overwrite permissions are needed. Save the policy and verify that the role's trust policy names the FlowCapture service principal. Confirm that the role has no identity-based policy for the bucket, and that default encryption on the bucket is set to AES256. Start delivery and check that the first Parquet file appears in the current day's partition within 15 minutes. A delivery status of PERMISSION_FAILED in FlowCapture generally points to a Principal ARN that does not match the role.

SentinelDrop writes vulnerability scan findings as newline-delimited JSON files, and this guide authorizes its IAM role SentinelDropWriter to place them in the S3 bucket example-scan-logs. The grant is placed only in an identity-based policy on the role; the bucket policy is not touched. Attach an inline policy with one Allow statement for s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::example-scan-logs/findings/*. Add a Condition using StringEquals on s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption with the value AES256, so only uploads that request server-side encryption are accepted. SentinelDrop sends this header by default when its encryption option is set to s3-managed. Findings are stored under keys such as findings/2026/11/21/scan-0042.ndjson, and each scan creates a new object. Verify that the bucket policy does not already grant the role anything, so the inline policy is the only source of access. Run a test scan against a staging host and confirm that the resulting object is listed with server-side encryption enabled. If uploads are rejected, check that the encryption option in SentinelDrop is not disabled.

The grant is placed only in the bucket's resource-based policy; the role itself has no S3 permissions. Add a statement with one Allow for s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::example-scan-logs/findings/*, with the Principal arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/SentinelDropWriter. Add a Condition using StringEquals on s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption with the value AES256, so only uploads that request server-side encryption are accepted. SentinelDrop sends this header by default when its encryption option is set to s3-managed. Findings are stored under keys such as findings/2026/11/21/scan-0042.ndjson, and each scan creates a new object. Verify that the role has no identity-based policy for this bucket, so the bucket policy statement is the only source of access. Run a test scan against a staging host and confirm that the resulting object is listed with server-side encryption enabled. If uploads are rejected, check that the encryption option in SentinelDrop is not disabled.

RunTrail collects build and test logs from CI runners and uploads them to the S3 bucket example-ci-logs, and this procedure grants its IAM role RunTrailUploader the required access. The role is assumed by runners through federation, and access is granted only by an identity-based policy on the role, leaving the bucket policy as it is. Create an inline policy with one Allow statement for s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::example-ci-logs/builds/*. Runners write one object per job, keyed as builds/project-name/build-number/job.log, and they never read logs back. A lifecycle rule on the bucket expires objects under builds/ after 30 days, so the role needs no delete permission. Set the maximum session duration of the role to one hour, which exceeds the longest expected job upload. Confirm that no bucket policy statement names RunTrailUploader or its assumed-role sessions. Run a sample pipeline and check that the log object appears under the correct project and build number. If an upload fails with AccessDenied, confirm that the runner is assuming RunTrailUploader and not a different role.

The role is assumed by runners through federation, and access is granted only by a statement in the bucket's resource-based policy, with no S3 permissions on the role. Add a statement to the bucket policy with one Allow for s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::example-ci-logs/builds/*, with the Principal arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/RunTrailUploader. Runners write one object per job, keyed as builds/project-name/build-number/job.log, and they never read logs back. A lifecycle rule on the bucket expires objects under builds/ after 30 days, so the role needs no delete permission. Set the maximum session duration of the role to one hour, which exceeds the longest expected job upload. Confirm that the role has no identity-based policy that mentions the bucket. Run a sample pipeline and check that the log object appears under the correct project and build number. If an upload fails with AccessDenied, confirm that the Principal ARN matches the role the runner is assuming.
